content: A capillary hemangioma, also referred to as an infantile hemangioma or strawberry hemangioma, is a raised, red, and lumpy area of skin that can appear anywhere on the body. However, approximately 83% of these lesions are found on the head or neck region. This type of birthmark typically becomes noticeable between one and four weeks after birth. It often grows rapidly during the early stages, then stops growing and gradually fades over time. In many cases, the hemangioma resolves naturally, with some disappearing by the age of 2, about 60% resolving by the age of 5, and 90–95% disappearing by the age of 9. Capillary hemangiomas are observed to occur five times more frequently in female infants compared to males and are most commonly seen in Caucasian populations. Additionally, infants with low birth weight have a 26% increased likelihood of developing a hemangioma. Although the appearance of this birthmark can be concerning to parents, physicians generally recommend allowing it to resolve on its own unless it interferes with critical functions, such as vision or breathing, by obstructing the nostrils.
